nodes.rationale: Rendered in the content area instead of ContentPlaceholder when the derived flag is true. The rail stays visible with zero tiles so the bell and gear remain reachable, and Settings can still open above it. A single centered column fits the 940x600 minimum window with no scroll.

nodes.label: Portal.tsx
nodes.rationale: The loading screen's ember portal extracted as a component; its keyframes move to a shared stylesheet imported by both the shell entry and the loading page, while loading.html keeps its inline critical-CSS copy.

nodes.label: Service picker grid
nodes.rationale: One 48px molten-squircle toggle per service in rail order, rendered as buttons with aria-pressed so it stays keyboard friendly; tapping a tile lights it with the active-tile gradient. Selection starts empty because enabling is a deliberate opt-in, and the confirm reads "Summon N services" in tabular numerals, disabled while nothing is selected.

nodes.label: Buried Settings modal bug
nodes.rationale: Disabling the active service from Settings looked like the modal closed, but settingsOpen stayed true: the handler called views.activate(next) unconditionally, and activate() re-adds the view at the top of the z-order, shows it, and focuses its webContents — so the modal was buried and unfocusable and Escape no longer reached it. The defect is not specific to Settings, so the fix is an invariant rather than a special case.

nodes.label: Overlay invariant: no view visible over a shell surface
nodes.rationale: Service views are native WebContentsViews layered above the shell renderer, so a visible view covers any shell surface. No code path may make one visible while settings, the switcher, or home is on screen — otherwise Home would get the same flash-over treatment Settings did.
nodes.norm_label: overlay invariant: no view visible over a shell surface

nodes.label: homeOpen shell surface
nodes.rationale: Joins switcherOpen and settingsOpen on MainState, ships in the ShellState snapshot, and is never persisted. The renderer keeps deriving (showWelcome = homeOpen || allDisabled), so homeOpen simply gives the all-disabled path a second, user-driven trigger. activeId: ServiceId | null with null meaning home was rejected: it reads well but changes the type of a field threaded through the menu, tray, badges, hibernation and resilience for no behavioral gain.

nodes.label: home:setOpen channel
nodes.rationale: Added to RendererToMain, R2M_CHANNELS and SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS — it carries no serviceId, so shell-only is the correct classification. Its handler mirrors settings:setOpen: set the flag, hideActive on open and showActive on close, state.touch(), and focus the shell on open so keyboard input reaches it.

nodes.label: anyOverlayOpen
nodes.rationale: A pure predicate over the three surface flags in src/main/lib/overlay-rules.ts, consulted at the call site so ipc-handlers.ts stays thin; resolveActivation is unchanged and only the presentation of its result changes.

nodes.label: views.activate show option
nodes.rationale: With show: false, activate creates the view if needed and moves it to the top of the z-order but leaves it hidden and skips webContents.focus(); showActive() reveals it when the surface closes. That is what makes the invariant enforceable rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: Rail leading sigil
nodes.rationale: A Portal-marked button prepended before the tiles with a hairline divider that keeps it out of the drag-to-reorder run. Head of the rail survives all three railPosition values, which the alternatives did not: a + tile after the last service moves as services are enabled and lands inside the reorder run, and a fourth icon in the bell/gear cluster reads as a setting rather than a place. Tiles gain active={!homeOpen && ...} so none reads as current while Home is up.

nodes.label: Home accelerator (CmdOrCtrl+0)
nodes.rationale: Registered as a menu accelerator rather than a globalShortcut, which is what makes it fire while a service WebContentsView has focus — the mechanism the numbered shortcuts already use. It sits above the service list so the Go menu reads as an ordered index, and it toggles like Cmd/Ctrl K. A plain item, not a checkbox: buildAppMenu rebuilds only on order and disabled changes, so a checkmark would go stale.

nodes.label: activateService clears homeOpen
nodes.rationale: Clearing the flag in the one existing entry point is what makes a rail tile, Cmd/Ctrl 1-6, the quick switcher, and a notification click all leave Home without each learning about it. syncOverlay and win.on('focus') simply grow a third term.

nodes.label: summonDelta
nodes.rationale: Lives in src/shared/welcome.ts beside buildDisabledPatch — process-agnostic and unit-testable — so the confirm button can name the change it is about to apply: "Summon 2 services", "Banish 1 service", "Summon 2 · Banish 1", or "No changes" when the delta is empty.

nodes.label: Seeded, staged picker
nodes.rationale: selected initializes from the live enabled set and re-seeds every time the screen becomes visible, so a discarded edit never survives to the next visit; on a fresh install the enabled set is empty, reproducing the old empty selection exactly. Nothing is written until confirm, and leaving by any other route discards. Banishing the last service is allowed because it produces exactly the fresh-install state on the screen the user is standing on, one click from recovery — blocking it would need a special-case disabled button that reads as a bug.

nodes.label: Escape leaves Home
nodes.rationale: Guarded the way SettingsView guards its own handler: only when Settings and the quick switcher are both closed, and only when at least one service is enabled.

nodes.label: Settings loses the enable toggle
nodes.rationale: Services keeps mute, never-hibernate and reload but lists only enabled services, with a "Manage services…" row that closes Settings and opens Home. This removes the bug class rather than patching it: composition (which services exist) and per-service behavior (how one acts) stop sharing a surface, so the enable toggle no longer lives behind a modal a view can cover.

nodes.label: Persist the surface on change, into Settings
nodes.rationale: Written the moment the surface changes rather than in before-quit, which survives force-quit, a renderer crash, and an OS restart — none of which run before-quit. conf writes synchronously and atomically over a ~1KB file, so a write per switch needs no debounce. A separate session-state store was rejected: a second file to construct, normalize, migrate and test for two scalars that fit an existing one.
nodes.norm_label: persist the surface on change, into settings

nodes.label: Settings.lastActiveId
nodes.rationale: The service focused when the app last closed, defaulting to null. A remembered runtime fact rather than a user preference — lastNotifiedVersion is the precedent.

nodes.label: Settings.lastHomeOpen
nodes.rationale: Records that Home was the surface on top at close — Home is a destination, Settings is a modal you pass through.

nodes.label: Two fields rather than a lastSurface union
nodes.rationale: Home is a layer over a service, not a replacement for one: closing it with Escape must reveal something underneath, so the service identity has to survive independently of whether Home was on top.
nodes.norm_label: two fields rather than a lastsurface union

nodes.label: normalize() leaves lastActiveId intact
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not extended to scrub an unknown lastActiveId: nulling it there would erase the difference between "recorded, but that service is gone" and "never recorded", which the resolver's rules depend on.

nodes.label: resolveStartupSurface
nodes.rationale: One pure resolver in src/main/lib/startup-surface.ts owns the launch surface, joining activation-rules.ts as vitest-covered decision logic so index.ts stays thin wiring. Rules in order: a null record falls back to firstEnabled and honours lastHomeOpen; an enabled recorded id restores; a disabled or catalog-absent id falls back to firstEnabled with homeOpen forced true.

nodes.label: StartupSurface
nodes.rationale: { activeId: ServiceId | null; homeOpen: boolean } — activeId is null only when no service can be activated at all, and homeOpen means Home covers the surface so the view must be activated hidden.

nodes.label: An unrestorable record opens Home, a missing one does not
nodes.rationale: A recorded service now disabled or gone means the app cannot honor the user's last position, so it hands the decision back with the Home picker rather than silently substituting another (user decision, 2026-08-10). But lastActiveId: null is a fresh install or a pre-field upgrade, not a failed restore — treating it as unrestorable would greet every existing user with Home once after upgrading for no information gained. The resolver still falls back to firstEnabled in that row so Escape out of Home lands on a real service.
nodes.norm_label: an unrestorable record opens home, a missing one does not

nodes.label: Startup activates hidden when Home is restored
nodes.rationale: views.activate(surface.activeId, { show: !surface.homeOpen }) is the load-bearing line: a visible view would bury Home exactly the way the settings-modal bug buried Settings. Focus needs no new guard because win.on('focus') and syncOverlay already read the flags set here, before the window finishes loading and the first broadcast fires.
nodes.norm_label: startup activates hidden when home is restored

nodes.label: rememberSurface
nodes.rationale: Writes both fields from live ctx.state rather than taking an id, which makes them impossible to write inconsistently and frees the settings:update call site from reasoning about whether next was applied. Three call sites: activateService, setHomeOpen, and the patch.disabled branch — the last called even when next is null, because that is precisely the unrestorable record that should reopen on Home.

nodes.label: setHomeOpen
nodes.rationale: homeOpen had two writers — the home:setOpen handler and toggleHome in menu.ts — already duplicating the same four steps. Rather than add rememberSurface to both and leave a fifth path free to forget it, the shared part moves into activate.ts. Focus deliberately stays at the call sites: the IPC handler focuses only when opening, toggleHome unconditionally, and collapsing that difference is a behavior change this design does not need.

nodes.label: Nested settings.update inside the handler is safe
nodes.rationale: SettingsStore.update writes through conf directly with no IPC round trip, nothing downstream in the handler reads the two new fields, and the closing ctx.broadcast() re-reads settings.get(). No new IPC channel means nothing to classify in SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS and no serviceId to validate.
nodes.norm_label: nested settings.update inside the handler is safe

nodes.label: Sections track the live set, the glow tracks the staged set
nodes.rationale: Section membership derives from the live enabled set and the molten face from the staged selection; keeping the two axes independent is the whole design, because a tile you just deselected stays exactly where your cursor left it and only loses its glow. A glowing tile under UNBOUND is the pending-summon signal and a dim tile under SUMMONED the pending-banish signal — no extra ring, dashed border or badge, since the confirm already names the counts. Confirming is the one moment tiles move.
nodes.norm_label: sections track the live set, the glow tracks the staged set

nodes.label: welcomeSections
nodes.rationale: A pure helper joining buildDisabledPatch and summonDelta in src/shared/welcome.ts, partitioning into summoned/unbound in rail order keyed on the LIVE enabled set, never the staged selection, so a tile never moves out from under the cursor mid-edit.

nodes.label: Empty sections keep their headers
nodes.rationale: "Nothing yet." under SUMMONED and "Every one is bound." under UNBOUND. Hiding the empty section was rejected because it would make a fresh install look exactly like the old flat row, so the first-run user never learns the two-section model before they need it. Counts are the tiles below them and change only on confirm — a count that moved while staging would contradict its own tiles. Labels stay Summoned/Unbound in source and are cased by CSS so a screen reader is not spelling out capitals.

nodes.label: Dispel button
nodes.rationale: Discard-in-place: it resets selected to the live enabled set — the same reseed the screen already performs on every visit — because Escape and the rail sigil both discard but also navigate away, so correcting a mis-click meant leaving Home and coming back. It reuses summonLabel's existing disabled flag (true exactly when the delta is empty), so no new predicate and no new test surface. Both buttons go dead together at rest; hiding Dispel when the edit is clean would shift the row's centering on every first click.

nodes.label: PickTile
nodes.rationale: Unchanged by the section split: its `on` prop keeps meaning "is staged on", so all four reachable states fall out of one rule — the face follows selected and nothing else.

nodes.label: Three tip cards that sell three things
nodes.rationale: Two of the three cards were keyboard cheatsheets, so two thirds of the screen's pitch was one idea. Dropping the cheatsheet framing makes room for claims true in code today: Chat only (recipe css plus views.refresh), Stays signed in (partition: persist:${id} per view, so logins survive restarts and no service reads another's cookies), and Quiet & light (ServiceTile badges direct counts and dots indirect traffic, and hibernationMinutes is 30). RailIcon and KeysIcon are deleted for LockIcon and MoonIcon; shortcut discovery survives in the hint line and Settings → Shortcuts.
nodes.norm_label: three tip cards that sell three things

nodes.label: The catalog ships in name order
nodes.rationale: SERVICES and DEFAULT_SETTINGS.order shipped in an ad-hoc order that encodes nothing a user can predict; only the array order changes, since ServiceId's declaration order is meaningless. No migration: normalize() preserves any persisted order, and rewriting a saved order would be the one thing a user cannot undo without redoing it by hand. A services.test.ts invariant asserting the names are localeCompare-sorted keeps the ad-hoc order from coming back.
nodes.norm_label: the catalog ships in name order

nodes.label: summonOrder
nodes.rationale: Newly summoned ids move to the end of order so an arrival lands where the user was last looking rather than jumping into the middle of a rail they have already arranged; a banished id keeps its slot and appends like any other arrival if re-summoned. Several at once append in name order, because selection is a Set carrying no click order and name order is what was on screen. summonDelta is untouched — it returns add in rail order for summonLabel's lengths, and conflating them would couple the button's caption to the ordering rule.

nodes.label: One settings:update patch for disabled + order
nodes.rationale: The existing handler already reads after.order for its teardown loop and for resolveActivation, and buildAppMenu already runs inside the patch.disabled branch keeping Cmd/Ctrl 1-9 aligned. A service:reorder followed by a settings:update would mean two broadcasts and a frame where order and enablement disagree. No new channel — settings:update is already shell-only and order is a key both the handler and normalize() accept.
nodes.norm_label: one settings:update patch for disabled + order

nodes.label: byName
nodes.rationale: Catalog ids in display-name order — the Unbound order and the order new arrivals append in. state.services is settings.order.map(serviceById) and already carries every catalog service with its name, so byName(state.services) needs no new IPC and no new main-process state.

nodes.label: Unbound is always in name order
nodes.rationale: Unbound followed settings.order, so reordering the rail silently reshuffled the pool of services you have not chosen — a list whose order carries no meaning and should therefore never move. The unchosen pool gets a predictable order instead, so the same service is always in the same place however the rail is arranged; Summoned keeps following settings.order because that list is the rail.
nodes.norm_label: unbound is always in name order

nodes.label: matchesQuery
nodes.rationale: Case-insensitive substring on the display name, deliberately not the quick switcher's fuzzyScore: that ranks candidates for a jump-to among a handful of enabled services where a stray match costs one glance, while this filters a visible grid where fuzzyScore("tg") surfacing Instagram beside Telegram reads as a bug and undermines trust in the filter. Results stay in name order with no score re-ranking, so tiles never reorder under the cursor as the query grows. A one-line swap back if substring proves too strict; the unit test pins the choice.

nodes.label: Unbound search control
nodes.rationale: Inline on the Unbound band's label row, right-aligned opposite the count, which costs no vertical height — the whole reason for that placement. Renders only when Unbound is non-empty, clear affordance only while the query is non-empty, aria-label since the band label is not a <label>, and no autofocus: Home is a place, not a modal, and stealing the keyboard on arrival would break Cmd/Ctrl 0 muscle memory and take arrow keys from the tiles. The query resets on every visit and after a confirm, like the selection reseed.

nodes.label: Two-step Escape ladder
nodes.rationale: A non-empty query clears and stops; otherwise Home closes as before. The query is read through a ref rather than an effect dependency so the listener registers once instead of on every keystroke and never closes over a stale value. Handling it on the input's own onKeyDown was rejected: stopping a React synthetic event from reaching a native window listener is a bug waiting to happen, and it would leave Escape closing Home while a filter is active whenever focus sits elsewhere.

nodes.label: Drag-to-reorder on Home
nodes.rationale: Reordering was only reachable from the rail — the one surface covered while Home is open. Summoned tiles mirror ServiceTile exactly and persist immediately through the existing service:reorder channel: reordering is non-destructive, so there is nothing to confirm and Summon/Dispel keep meaning enable/disable only. The rail visibly re-ordering behind Home is the confirmation. Unbound tiles are not draggable — that section has no order to edit.

nodes.label: moveTo
nodes.rationale: The rail's inline index arithmetic extracted to a tested helper rather than copied to a second surface. Splice semantics are preserved verbatim including the index-shift quirk (to is resolved before the removal, so a forward move lands one slot short) — the extraction adds a test, not a fix. Both surfaces reorder the full settings.order and the disabled ids between the endpoints ride along, exactly as on the rail today.

nodes.label: Board layout (header / bands / pinned footer)
nodes.rationale: Three directions were measured in a real Chromium layout pass, not estimated: at 8 services all three fit the 748px budget, but at a Ferdium-sized 62 services the compact column wants 1040px and the two-column split 852px, while the board's home area scrollHeight still equals its clientHeight. The board wins because no-scrolling is a property of the layout rather than a coincidence of content — only the tile areas grow, and they grow into their own scroll containers. The header and action bar never move, so the confirm is always on screen instead of being the first thing to fall off the bottom. Width was never the constraint, which is why the split gains nothing at scale.

nodes.label: Two states, one skeleton
nodes.rationale: On a fresh install the compact header is replaced by the welcome block (portal, title, tagline, tip cards) and the single band reads "Choose your services"; once anything is summoned the tips give their space back and the Summoned band appears. The tips are onboarding — they earn their space exactly once, and reclaiming it is what gives the steady state room while showing more tiles.

nodes.label: Board sizing rules
nodes.rationale: The board is flex-1 min-h-0 under an already-definite height chain so a percentage cap resolves; Summoned is capped at max-h-[46%] because without it a long summoned list crowds Unbound out of the board entirely; Unbound is flex-[0_1_auto] so it shrinks rather than pushing the footer; each band's tile area is the scroll container so its scrollHeight is the honest measure. Tile labels truncate to one line — a two-line label pushes its whole row taller and breaks the grid. The first-run stack centers with margin: auto, the standing fix for justify-center plus overflow-y-auto clipping the top of overflowing content instead of scrolling to it (a latent bug in today's screen).

nodes.label: welcome/ServiceBand.tsx
nodes.rationale: Label row, optional aside slot, scroll area, empty state. Keeps the welcome-section-summoned/-unbound testids so existing e2e selectors survive; on a fresh install the single "Choose your services" band carries welcome-section-unbound because it is the unbound band relabelled, so selectors need not know which state they are in.

nodes.label: welcome/WelcomeIntro.tsx
nodes.rationale: Portal, title, tagline and tip cards, first run only, carrying data-testid="welcome-intro" — the hook that replaces welcome.spec.ts's "Nothing yet." assertion, since the first-run state has no Summoned band.

nodes.label: The rail overflows before Home does
nodes.rationale: At 32px per tile plus a 6px gap, roughly 30 summoned services fill a 1280px rail and the rest fall off the end. Home survives 62 services in this design; the rail does not survive summoning them — a separate change. Compact 48px unlabelled tiles roughly halve the height cost and are the obvious next lever past ~150 services, so they are not built now.
nodes.norm_label: the rail overflows before home does

nodes.label: Instagram chat service
nodes.rationale: The eighth service: id instagram, url https://www.instagram.com/direct/inbox/ (the chat surface directly, never the feed), colour #E4405F, waitForReady: true, placed after messenger and shipping disabled. Like facebook.com the site is mostly not chat — feed, reels, explore, profiles — so it needs the full chat-only treatment.

nodes.label: normalize() catalog-position slotting
nodes.rationale: Ids missing from a persisted order slot in at their catalog position — right after the nearest catalog predecessor the user already has — rather than appending, so instagram lands beside messenger on existing installs too. Revised the same day after a live smoke test showed it appended to the end of the rail.

nodes.label: chatPaths: ['/direct']
nodes.rationale: Covers /direct/inbox/ and /direct/t/<thread>. Login flows at /accounts/login/ never reach a chat path, so they are never snapped back.

nodes.label: meta-unread.ts shared Meta heuristics
nodes.rationale: Instagram web shares Meta's chat-list DOM language with facebook.com/messages — bold text, a small blue dot, an "Unread" screen-reader string — so messenger's unread-row detection and banner-text extraction move verbatim into a shared module parameterized by thread-link selector and a link-to-row resolver. Messenger keeps [role='row']; instagram resolves [role='listitem'], [role='row'] with the link itself as fallback. Messenger's behavior is unchanged and its existing fixture tests are the proof.

nodes.label: Instagram synthNotification
nodes.rationale: Instagram DMs never notify in-page — delegated to browser push, which Electron cannot receive — so sender and preview come from the first unread row's dir="auto" spans with the time suffix stripped, mirroring messenger's.

nodes.label: hideChrome recipe hook
nodes.rationale: An optional hook returning Element[], run by the runner every tick with an idempotent display:none inside try/catch so SPA re-renders get re-hidden. Introduced because two live smoke tests showed no static selector survives for Instagram's nav rail: it is hash-classed, half its icons are role=button, and it carries no nav/role=navigation landmark. A throw must never break counting.

nodes.label: Structural nav-rail computation
nodes.rationale: The rail is computed as the branch holding the DM nav link (one not inside main) that sits beside main. Login pages render no main, so they are untouched, and a layout that nests the nav inside main hides nothing rather than risking the chat surface — failing closed on the surface that matters.

nodes.label: Rail space reclaim
nodes.rationale: Because the rail is position:fixed, hiding it leaves its reserved width as a dead column in two shapes. So hideChrome also walks main up to the layout root inclusive plus the single-child wrapper spine below main, zeroing any rail-sized (>=40px) left margin/padding/offset — pane-internal paddings are far smaller and survive — and stretching any element under-filling its parent by >=40px, which is the width: calc(100% - rail) leftover that otherwise strands a blank strip at the pane's right edge.

nodes.label: StyleX atomic class .x132t2bv
nodes.rationale: A live inspection found this padded wrapper (padding-inline-start: 72px) outside the original ancestor chain. The recipe css zeroes its padding directly because StyleX hashes are derived from the single declaration they carry and so survive rebuilds far better than component classes, with the structural reclaim as the fallback if the hash ever rotates.

nodes.label: pointer-events inerting of off-chat links
nodes.rationale: pointer-events: none on a[href^='/']:not([href^='/direct']) — thread-header avatar and username, @mentions, shared posts — instead of letting them navigate and then snap back. Messenger gains the same inert rule for its profile links, both gated on the chat surface being mounted so login and captcha pages stay untouched.

nodes.label: Instagram calibration caveat
nodes.rationale: Selectors follow Meta's messenger DOM language but are uncalibrated against a live logged-in session (tiktok precedent), noted in the recipe until a live login pass; ALLOWED_HOSTS verification needs the same session.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_HOSTS.instagram
nodes.rationale: www.instagram.com, instagram.com, accounts.instagram.com, plus www.facebook.com/facebook.com for the Log-in-with-Facebook bounce. VERIFY LIVE before wiring enforcement.

nodes.label: macOS copy-cursor badge defect
nodes.rationale: Neither tile surface set effectAllowed or dropEffect, so Chromium fell back to copy — drawn by macOS as a green ⊕ badge faded in on the window server's schedule, a beat behind the pointer. Semantically wrong for a reorder and the slowest-updating thing on screen. Worse, no dragenter/dragleave/dragend handlers existed on either tile, so order changed only at drop: the OS badge was the sole moving element, which is exactly why the gesture read as laggy. Setting both effects to move removes the badge but leaves the gesture silent rather than slow.

nodes.label: Reorder.Group / pointer-driven reorder
nodes.rationale: motion's Reorder.Group/Item replace the HTML5 handlers on both tiles, in devDependencies since electron-vite bundles the renderer and it is never in the packaged node_modules. With no OS drag session there is no OS cursor to lag: the tile under the pointer is the real tile transformed at frame rate, and the neighbours animating into the vacated slot make the resulting order self-evident before release — an insertion line describes the outcome, a live gap is the outcome. Axis detection from item positions supports Home's wrapping grid, the one property that could have disqualified the direction; draggable, onDragStart/onDragOver/onDrop and the text/goetia-service data type are deleted. cursor-grab/grabbing survives and now holds for the whole gesture.

nodes.label: Draft order, committed once on drag end
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group is controlled and fires onReorder on every crossing, not on release — wired straight to service:reorder, one drag across three tiles would be three conf writes, three MainState broadcasts, three rail re-renders and three app-menu rebuilds, the per-tick broadcast CLAUDE.md forbids. So the drag runs entirely in the renderer and reaches main once, sending `shown` rather than `draft` so a drag ending where it started is a harmless no-op instead of a crash on null. The draft is cleared when the broadcast carrying the new order arrives, not on commit — clearing on commit would render one frame of the pre-drag order during the round trip, a visible snap-back exactly when the drop should have taken. Since the arriving order equals the draft, clearing is visually a no-op, and any other mid-drag order change trips the same condition and drops the draft rather than letting a stale local array fight broadcast state.
nodes.norm_label: draft order, committed once on drag end

nodes.label: applySubsetOrder
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group knows only the ids it renders while settings.order holds the whole catalog including disabled ids, and moveTo's (from, to) signature cannot express merging a finished array back in. The `known` filter is not decoration: without it an unknown id still enters the slots set and shifts the cursor, so full=[A,B,C], subset=[Z,C,A] yields [Z,B,C]; filtering first makes matching slots equal moved.length exactly. Deliberate behaviour change — moveTo spliced the full array so disabled ids between endpoints rode along, while this pins every non-member to its absolute index; the old behaviour was an implementation side effect, and a hidden id shifting because of a visible drag is unobservable and cannot be reasoned about from the screen.

nodes.label: Rail Reorder.Group wiring
nodes.rationale: The <nav> also holds the Home button, a divider and the bell/gear cluster, but Reorder.Group measures its own children to detect axis and compute crossings — so the tiles move into their own flex box, which becomes the group, keeping the same gap and alignment so the rendered result is unchanged. axis is set explicitly rather than detected because a rail holding a single service has no second item to infer from; Home's grid needs axis="xy" because it wraps and a tile dragged to another row moves on both axes.

nodes.label: Transform ownership (Motion vs Tailwind scale)
nodes.rationale: ServiceTile's scale-105 sits on the very button that becomes the Reorder.Item, and Motion writes transform on the element it drags, so Tailwind's scale and Motion's translate would overwrite each other. The active scale moves into Motion's hands as animate={{ scale }} and scale-105 leaves stateClasses. PickTile needs no equivalent change: its scale-105 is on the inner face span.

nodes.label: Trailing-click guard
nodes.rationale: HTML5 drag-and-drop suppressed the click that follows a completed drag; pointer drag does not, so releasing on Home would toggle that service off and on the rail would activate it — a drag that silently performs the tile's click action is worse than the lag being fixed. onDragStart sets a ref that onClick consumes and clears before the tile's own handler runs, and Motion fires onDragStart only past its drag threshold, so an ordinary click never sets it.

nodes.label: layoutScroll on the scrolling band
nodes.rationale: Motion's projection needs layoutScroll on a scrollable ancestor to correct for scroll offset; without it a drag inside a scrolled Summoned band computes crossings against stale rects. It only bites once Summoned overflows its max-h-[46%], which is why it is easy to ship broken.

nodes.label: Order-insensitive enabledKey
nodes.rationale: enabledKey joined the enabled ids in settings.order, so it was order-sensitive and a reorder changed it without changing the enabled set — dropping a tile on Home therefore discarded whatever the user had staged for Summon and cleared the search box. The reseed is about membership, not order (its own comment says so), so sorting before joining makes the key say that; the consumer splits it back into a Set, so sorted order is immaterial. A summon, dispel or catalog change still trips it; a pure reorder no longer does. Shipping a pleasant reorder onto a reorder that eats staged work would make the bug more reachable, not less.

nodes.label: What the drag looks like
nodes.rationale: whileDrag scale 1.1 plus a raised shadow, neighbours settling on Motion's default spring; badge, mute, crash and stale decorations ride along as the tile's children and the on/active gradient is untouched. No landing pulse and no band hint — the reflow is the confirmation, and the rail reordering behind Home is the second one.

nodes.label: Pointer drag makes the reorder path e2e-testable
nodes.rationale: Pointer-driven drag is reachable from mouse.down/move/up, which HTML5 drag-and-drop never was — so the renderer → service:reorder → main → broadcast path can be covered end to end for the first time, which is the e2e-on-wiring the definition of done asks for.
nodes.norm_label: pointer drag makes the reorder path e2e-testable

nodes.label: Instagram recipe fixture
nodes.rationale: The count oracle for the instagram recipe: five listitem rows of thread links, of which exactly three carry an unread signal.

nodes.label: Three unread signals (bold, blue dot, "Unread" text)
nodes.rationale: bao.tran is bold (font-weight 700), minh.le carries the blue rgb(0,149,246) dot deliberately placed outside the anchor so the link-to-row resolver is exercised, and chi.nguyen carries the screen-reader "Unread" span — three direct. an.pham's green rgb(18,173,43) presence dot and the plain read rows must count nothing.
nodes.norm_label: three unread signals (bold, blue dot, "unread" text)

nodes.label: #rail nav branch
nodes.rationale: Holds a /direct/inbox/ nav link plus role=button icons and sits beside the branch containing <main>, which is exactly the shape the structural rail computation looks for; the role=button entries stand in for the icons that carry no stable selector.

nodes.label: Rail-sized offsets (#content margin, #inner padding)
nodes.rationale: #content's 72px left margin and #inner's 72px left padding are the >=40px rail-sized offsets the space reclaim must zero, while main's 16px padding is the pane-internal padding it must leave alone — the fixture encodes both halves of that threshold.

nodes.label: Slack recipe fixture
nodes.rationale: The count oracle for the slack recipe, with the sidebar mounted (.p-channel_sidebar plus data-qa="workspace_sidebar") so ready() is true; the title "Slack - Goetia HQ" carries no (n), so the badge path rather than the title fallback is what is measured.

nodes.label: Mention-badge rows (2 + 1 → direct 3)
nodes.rationale: alice and bob are unread rows carrying .c-mention_badge values that sum to the direct count, and being badge-bearing they must be excluded from indirect so a mentioned channel is not counted twice.

nodes.label: Badge-less unread channels (indirect 2)
nodes.rationale: general and launch are unread with no badge, which is exactly the indirect signal; the read #archive row anchors the negative case.

nodes.label: Muted unread row that counts nothing
nodes.rationale: #noise carries both --unread and --muted, pinning the :not(--muted) half of the indirect selector.
nodes.norm_label: muted unread row that counts nothing

nodes.norm_label: flat white camera glyph on crimson squircle

nodes.norm_label: slack octothorpe brand mark (white on aubergine)
